Jordan —

Quick answers to your two asks from a technical perspective:
1) Dedicated capacity: yes — Dedicated pools are single-tenant from a customer workload perspective (reserved GPU pools) and can be deployed in isolated subnets. We support VPC peering or IPsec tunnels depending on cloud provider. For strict network isolation we recommend Private VPC since the control plane is logically separated and can be placed behind your VPC endpoints.

2) SOC 2 / KMS: attaching our SOC 2 evidence checklist and an excerpt of our KMS runbook. Customer-managed KMS is supported via external key management (bring-your-own KMS) for both Private VPC and, with additional contractual controls, for Dedicated. Key rotation flow with BYOK relies on your KMS rotating keys and Redwood rewrapping per the agreed procedure — I can walk through the exact steps in the security sync.

Notes / tradeoffs to be aware of:
- Dedicated (fastest time-to-ship): lower operational overhead, Redwood manages control plane but we offer strict network isolation and contractual commitments. Good for teams that need predictable throughput quickly.
- Private VPC (maximum isolation): customer control plane, full network boundary separation, works best if your procurement/compliance requires customer-managed control plane.

Next steps:
- If you confirm pilot scope (data sets + whether BYOK is required for pilot), I’ll schedule a 60-min security/design review next week.

Attachments: soc2-evidence-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
